answerable.question: What is the community solar credit rate for 2024?
answerable.answer:
Members receive a bill credit at the community solar credit rate, which was set at 11.7 cents per kilowatt-hour for 2024. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 3]

Credit rate: the value per kilowatt-hour assigned to community solar production, set annually by the state utility commission. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 8]

answerable.question: Is there an enrollment fee?
answerable.answer: There is no enrollment fee and no credit check. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 2]

answerable.question: How much notice is required to cancel a subscription?
answerable.answer: Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle and require 30 days' written notice. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 2]

answerable.question: What is the maximum residential share size?
answerable.answer: The minimum share size is 1 kilowatt and the maximum residential share is 25 kilowatts. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 4]

answerable.question: When is planned maintenance on the array scheduled?
answerable.answer:
Planned maintenance, including panel cleaning and inverter inspection, is scheduled twice a year, in April and October, and typically reduces output for no more than two days. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

Maintenance, Performance and Outages The Meadowbrook array is maintained by Helios Field Services under a 20-year operations contract. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

answerable.question: What happens if the array produces less than 90 percent of its expected output?
answerable.answer:
The program includes a performance guarantee: if the array produces less than 90 percent of its expected annual output for reasons other than weather, members' subscription payments for that year are reduced proportionally. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

In 2023 the array achieved 96 percent of its expected output. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

answerable.question: Can I keep my subscription if I move to a new address?
answerable.answer:
Moving, Transfers and Account Changes Members who move within the Verdant Power & Light service territory can keep their subscription by submitting a transfer form with the new service address at least 14 days before the move. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 6]

A subscription may be transferred to another person, such as a new homeowner or a family member, provided the recipient is eligible and signs a new subscription agreement. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 6]

Members who move outside the service territory must cancel their subscription because credits can only be applied to accounts with the local utility. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 6]

answerable.question: What are the phone support hours?
answerable.answer:
Member Support and Dispute Resolution The member support team is available by phone Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 7]

to 6:00 p.m., and by email at any time. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 7]

Unplanned outages lasting more than 24 hours are reported to members by email within 48 hours, and a status page shows live production data. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

answerable.question: How was the solar array funded?
answerable.answer: The array was financed through a combination of member subscriptions, a state clean energy grant of 3.2 million dollars, and a loan from the Verdant Community Bank. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 8]

answerable.question: How many active members does the program have?
answerable.answer:
As of January 2024 the program has 2,350 active members and a waiting list of about 400 households. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 1]

The program is administered by the Orion Energy Cooperative, which is governed by a seven-member board elected by the membership every two years. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 1]

answerable.question: Within how many days must a billing dispute be submitted?
answerable.answer: Billing disputes must be submitted in writing within 60 days of the statement date. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 7]

answerable.question: What is the total capacity of the Meadowbrook array?
answerable.answer:
Members subscribe to a share of a shared solar array located at the Meadowbrook site, which has a total capacity of 4.8 megawatts. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 1]

Billing and Bill Credits Each month, the Meadowbrook array's output is measured by the utility and allocated to members according to their share size. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 3]

Maintenance, Performance and Outages The Meadowbrook array is maintained by Helios Field Services under a 20-year operations contract. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

answerable.question: What processing fee applies to credit card payments?
answerable.answer: A 3 percent processing fee applies to credit card payments. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 3]

answerable.question: Who maintains the Meadowbrook array?
answerable.answer:
Maintenance, Performance and Outages The Meadowbrook array is maintained by Helios Field Services under a 20-year operations contract. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 5]

Members subscribe to a share of a shared solar array located at the Meadowbrook site, which has a total capacity of 4.8 megawatts. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 1]

Billing and Bill Credits Each month, the Meadowbrook array's output is measured by the utility and allocated to members according to their share size. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 3]

answerable.question: Are renters eligible to join the solar program?
answerable.answer: Renters are eligible because the subscription is tied to the electricity account, not the property. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 1]

answerable.question: How long was the typical waiting period in 2023?
answerable.answer: The typical waiting period in 2023 was between 20 and 45 days. [orion_solar_handbook.pdf, p. 2]

answerable.question: How much does a non-resident library card cost?
answerable.answer:
Residents of other communities may purchase a non-resident card for 45 dollars per year. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 1]

A library card is free for anyone who lives, works, or attends school in the City of Lumen. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 1]

A replacement card costs 2 dollars. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 1]

answerable.question: How long can I borrow a DVD?
answerable.answer:
Borrowing Limits and Loan Periods Cardholders may have up to 50 items checked out at one time, including no more than 10 DVDs and 5 video games. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 2]

DVDs, video games, and items from the Lucky Day collection are loaned for one week. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 2]

Books, audiobooks, and music CDs are loaned for three weeks. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 2]

answerable.question: Does the library charge overdue fines?
answerable.answer: Fines, Fees and Lost Items Since January 2022 the library no longer charges daily overdue fines on any materials. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 3]

answerable.question: How many holds can I place at one time?
answerable.answer: Holds and Interlibrary Loan Patrons may place up to 10 holds at a time on items owned by the library. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 4]

answerable.question: How much does 3D printing cost at the library?
answerable.answer:
3D printing costs 10 cents per gram of filament, and laser cutting is 1 dollar per 10 minutes of cutting time. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 5]

The Makerspace at Central Library offers a 3D printer, a laser cutter, and sewing machines. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 5]

Printing costs 15 cents per page for black and white and 50 cents per page for color; scanning and faxing are free. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 6]

answerable.question: How much does color printing cost per page?
answerable.answer: Printing costs 15 cents per page for black and white and 50 cents per page for color; scanning and faxing are free. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 6]

answerable.question: What is the interlibrary loan fee?
answerable.answer:
Interlibrary loan items usually arrive within one to three weeks and are loaned for the period set by the lending library, often two to four weeks. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 4]

Materials not owned by Lumen Public Library can be requested through interlibrary loan for a fee of 3 dollars per request, which covers return shipping. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 4]

Interlibrary loan items cannot be renewed online; patrons must call the Reference Desk to request an extension. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 4]

answerable.question: How long are public computer sessions?
answerable.answer: Public computers are available at every branch and may be used for two-hour sessions, with an extension granted if no one is waiting. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 6]

answerable.question: How much does a replacement library card cost?
answerable.answer: A replacement card costs 2 dollars. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 1]

answerable.question: What is the processing fee for a lost item?
answerable.answer:
An item that is 45 days overdue is considered lost, and the replacement cost plus a 5 dollar processing fee is charged to the account. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 3]

If the item is later returned in good condition, the replacement cost is refunded but the processing fee is not. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 3]

answerable.question: How many branches does the library operate?
answerable.answer: The library operates four branches: Central, Riverside, Oakmont, and Hilltop. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 1]

answerable.question: How much do meeting rooms cost for for-profit businesses?
answerable.answer: For-profit businesses may reserve meeting rooms for 40 dollars per hour. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 5]

answerable.question: How long is a hold kept at the pickup branch?
answerable.answer: When a hold is ready, the patron is notified by email or text message and the item is kept at the chosen pickup branch for 7 days. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 4]

answerable.question: How many digital items can I borrow per month?
answerable.answer:
Each cardholder may borrow up to 15 digital items per month. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 6]

Borrowing Limits and Loan Periods Cardholders may have up to 50 items checked out at one time, including no more than 10 DVDs and 5 video games. [lumen_library_policy.pdf, p. 2]
